1.6 Pullbacks of categories

We will now axiomatize the pullback of two functors \(f\colon C \to E\) and \(g\colon D \to E\) of categories. This will be similar to the axiom for the product \(C \times D\), but it is more involved due to the fact that we need to record compatibilities with the structure maps to \(E\).

Definition 1.6.1. Consider two functors \(f\colon C \to E\) and \(g\colon D \to E\). Given a category \(T\), we define a cone diagram on \(T\) to be a triple \(c = (t_C,t_D,\tau )\) consisting of functors \(t_C\colon T \to C\) and \(t_D\colon T \to D\) together with an identification \(\tau \colon f \circ t_C = g \circ t_D\). In other words, a cone diagram consists of a commutative square of the form

Agda A cone diagram

Cone

Definition, checked

  record Cone {C D E : CAT Γ} (f : MAP C E) (g : MAP D E) (T : CAT Γ) : Set m where
    field
      left : MAP T C
      right : MAP T D
      match : (f ∘ left) =₁ (g ∘ right)

We call \(T\) the cone point of the diagram. Given another cone diagram \(c' = (t'_C,t'_D,\tau ')\), an identification of cone diagrams \(c = c'\) is a triple \(\Phi \colon (\varphi _C,\varphi _D,H)\), where \(\varphi _C\colon t_C = t'_C\) and \(\varphi _D\colon t_D = t'_D\) are identifications, and \(H\) is an identification \[ \tau '\circ (f\star \varphi _C)=(g\star \varphi _D)\circ \tau . \] In particular, a comparison of cones needs to be compatible with the identifications forming the commutative square. In turn, if \(\Psi \colon (\psi _C,\psi _D,G)\) is another identification of cone diagrams \(c = c'\), we say that \(\Phi \) and \(\Psi \) are identified if there are identifications \(\varphi _C = \psi _C\) and \(\varphi _D = \psi _D\) under which \(H\) becomes identified with \(G\).

Agda An isomorphism of cone diagrams

ConeIdentification

Definition, checked

  record ConeIdentification (X : CAT Γ) {C D E T : CAT Γ}
    {f : MAP C E} {g : MAP D E} (s t : Cone f g T) : Set m where
    open Terms.Equalities X using (_＝_)
    field
      left : Cone.left s ＝ Cone.left t
      right : Cone.right s ＝ Cone.right t
      compatible : SquareCell₌ (f ◁ left) (g ◁ right)
        (const (Cone.match s)) (const (Cone.match t))

Agda Identifying cone comparisons

ConeIdentificationEquality

Definition, checked

  record ConeIdentificationEquality {X C D E T : CAT Γ}
    {f : MAP C E} {g : MAP D E} {s t : Cone f g T}
    (Φ Ψ : ConeIdentification X s t) : Set m where
    field
      left : ConeIdentification.left Φ =₁ ConeIdentification.left Ψ
      right : ConeIdentification.right Φ =₁ ConeIdentification.right Ψ

    left-boundary :
      (const (Cone.match t) ∙ (f ◁ ConeIdentification.left Φ)) =₁
      (const (Cone.match t) ∙ (f ◁ ConeIdentification.left Ψ))
    left-boundary = comp₌-cong (id₌ (const (Cone.match t))) (postWhisker f ◁ left)

    right-boundary :
      ((g ◁ ConeIdentification.right Φ) ∙ const (Cone.match s)) =₁
      ((g ◁ ConeIdentification.right Ψ) ∙ const (Cone.match s))
    right-boundary = comp₌-cong (postWhisker g ◁ right) (id₌ (const (Cone.match s)))

    field
      compatible : (ConeIdentification.compatible Ψ ∙ left-boundary) =₂
        (right-boundary ∙ ConeIdentification.compatible Φ)

Given a functor \(s\colon S \to T\) and a cone diagram \(c = (t_C,t_D,\tau )\) on \(T\) we obtain another cone diagram \(s^*(c) := (t_C \circ s, t_D \circ s, \tau \ast \id _s)\) on \(S\). Similarly, every identification \(s_1 = s_2\) of functors \(S \to T\) induces an identification \(s^*_1(c) = s^*_2(c)\) of cone diagrams.

Agda Restricting a cone

cone-restrict

Definition, checked

  cone-restrict : {C D E S T : CAT Γ} {f : MAP C E} {g : MAP D E}
    → MAP S T → Cone f g T → Cone f g S
Proof / implementation
  cone-restrict {f = f} {g} r s = record
    { left = Cone.left s ∘ r
    ; right = Cone.right s ∘ r
    ; match = comp-assoc r (Cone.right s) g ∙
        ((Cone.match s ▷ r) ∙ (comp-assoc r (Cone.left s) f) ⁻¹) }

Axiom B.6 (Pullback of categories). For functors \(f\colon C\to E\) and \(g\colon D\to E\), there is a category \(C\times _E D\), called their pullback or fiber product, with projections \(\pr _1\colon C\times _E D\to C\) and \(\pr _2\colon C\times _E D\to D\), and an identification \(\tau _{\univ }\colon f\pr _1= g\pr _2\). Given \(a\colon T\to C\), \(b\colon T\to D\) and \(\tau \colon fa= gb\), there is a functor \((a,b)_\tau \colon T\to C\times _E D\) equipped with projection comparisons \(c\colon \pr _1(a,b)_\tau = a\) and \(d\colon \pr _2(a,b)_\tau = b\) and an identification \[ \tau \circ (f\star c)= (g\star d)\circ (\tau _{\univ }\star (a,b)_\tau ). \] If \(C,D,E\) are animae, then \(C\times _E D\) is an anima.

Agda The chosen pullback category

For any \(h,k\colon T\to C\times _E D\), the projection-induced functor \[ (h= k)\longrightarrow (\pr _1 h=\pr _1 k) \times _{(f\pr _1 h= g\pr _2 k)} (\pr _2 h=\pr _2 k) \] is an equivalence; here the two functors defining the pullback on the right are \[ \alpha \longmapsto (\tau _{\univ }\star k)\circ (f\star \alpha ), \qquad \beta \longmapsto (g\star \beta )\circ (\tau _{\univ }\star h). \] Interchange with \(\tau _{\univ }\) identifies their composites with the two projections from \((h= k)\) and thereby defines the displayed functor.

The final clause uses the pullback construction, now applied to three animae of identifications. In term notation the factorization is written \[ x:T\vdash (a(x),b(x))_{\tau (x)}:C\times _E D. \] The subscript may be omitted when it is clear from context, or left implicit to simplify notation. An identification between two such expressions is written \((\alpha (x),\beta (x))_{\eta (x)}\), where \(\eta \) is the identification between the two composites in the middle anima of identifications of the axiom.

Proof

Proof. We first show that applying \(\Map (T,-)\) to the chosen pullback \(C\times _E D\) results in a pullback square. Postcomposition with the two projections and whiskering with \(\tau _{\univ }\) gives a comparison functor \[ \Map (T,C\times _E D)\longrightarrow \Map (T,C)\times _{\Map (T,E)}\Map (T,D). \] For an inverse, let \(P\) be the anima on the right. Uncurrying the projections to \(\Map (T,C)\) and \(\Map (T,D)\) gives maps from \(P \times T\) to \(C\) and \(D\). Moreover, the identification in the commutative square for \(C \times _E D\) results in an identification of two functors \(P \times T \to E\). The pullback axiom thus supplies a functor from \(P \times T\) to \(C\times _E D\), with the projection comparisons and their compatibility with the squares. Currying gives a candidate inverse functor \(P \to \Map (T,C \times _D E)\).

Proof. This is a special case of Proposition 1.6.3. □

Exercise 1.6.5 (Exercise 1.9.4 (outside selection)). Show that the fiber product is commutative, associative and unital: for functors \(C\to \Gamma \), \(D \to \Gamma \) and \(B \to \Gamma \), there are preferred equivalences \[ C \times _{\Gamma } D \iso D \times _{\Gamma } C, \qquad B \times _{\Gamma } (C \times _{\Gamma } D) \iso (B \times _{\Gamma } C) \times _{\Gamma } D, \qquad C \times _{\Gamma } \Gamma \iso C. \]

Proof. We need to show that the induced functor \[ (C \times _{\Gamma } \Gamma ') \sqcup (D \times _{\Gamma } \Gamma ') \to (C \sqcup D) \times _\Gamma \Gamma ' \] is an equivalence. Lemma 1.6.18. The following two conditions are equivalent:

Agda Contractibility of the two-point coproduct

two-contractible-implies-all

Derivation, checked

  two-contractible-implies-all : IsContractible (One ⊔ One)
    → (C : CAT Γ) → IsContractible C
Proof / implementation
  two-contractible-implies-all two-contractible C =
    contractible-source to-zero (into-zero-isEquiv to-zero) zero-contractible
    where
    inclusion : MAP One (One ⊔ One)
    inclusion = in₁
    inclusion-isEquiv : IsEquiv inclusion
    inclusion-isEquiv = equiv-cancel-left inclusion (terminate (One ⊔ One))
      two-contractible
      (equiv-transport (terminal-identification (id One) _ ) (id-isEquiv One))
    initial-terminal-isEquiv : IsEquiv (initiate One)
    initial-terminal-isEquiv = left-isEquiv-from-isPullback
      inclusion-isEquiv (disjoint-cone One One) (disjoint-isPullback One One)
    zero-contractible : IsContractible Zero
    zero-contractible = equiv-transport
      (terminal-identification (initiate One) (terminate Zero)) initial-terminal-isEquiv
    to-zero : MAP C Zero
    to-zero = IsEquiv.inverse initial-terminal-isEquiv ∘ terminate C

(1)

The category \(* \sqcup *\) is contractible;

(2)

Every category is contractible.

Proof

Proof. It is clear that (2) implies (1). Conversely, assume that \(* \sqcup *\) is contractible, i.e. that the map \(* \sqcup * \to *\) is an equivalence. Since this map admits a section given by the left inclusion \(l\colon * = * \sqcup \emptyset \hookrightarrow * \sqcup *\), it follows that \(l\) is an equivalence. In particular, its fiber over the right point must be contractible. Since this fiber is the empty category \(\emptyset \) by Corollary 1.6.15, we see that the map \(\emptyset \to *\) is an equivalence, and it follows from taking the product with any category \(C\) that also \(\emptyset \to C\) is an equivalence. By 2-out-of-3 this implies that \(C\) is contractible. □

If \(v\) and \(w\) are embeddings and the composite square is a pullback square, then also the top square is a pullback square.

Proof

Proof. Consider the following commutative diagram:

Since \(w\) is an embedding, the map \(E' \times _E D \to D\) is an embedding by Lemma 1.6.23. Since \(v\colon D' \to D\) is also an embedding, it thus follows from Lemma 1.6.26 that the map \((g',v)\colon D' \to E' \times _E D\) is an embedding, and thus by Lemma 1.6.25 the top left square is a pullback square. Since the right bottom square and right outer rectangle are pullback squares, so is the top right square by the pasting law Lemma 1.6.11. Another instance of Lemma 1.6.11 shows that the outer rectangle is a pullback square, as desired. □
